agent_explanations_oldest_first.text: The regime switch is written late. Almost all of the regime difference along the layer-20 direction is added in layers 16 to 20 (17 to 26% each), with nothing before layer 13. Within the MLPs it is fairly concentrated: L16 neuron 180 carries 41% of layer 16's MLP contribution and #3729 another 24%, and L17 #3621 carries 19% of layer 17's. All three push toward the LaTeX regime. This gives a causal test of whether the regime choice controls accuracy. If I amplify these three neurons' down columns, more problems should open with "Let $N$...". If regime-0 problems then behave like regime-1 problems, accuracy should rise a little, but loops may rise too. Before editing, I'll look at their activations at the last prompt token by regime, to confirm the sign, size and selectivity that the edit relies on. Then I'll save a ×3 down-column scaling of the three and record it in the notes, ready for a paired generation pass on fresh DEV problems (DEV[512:768]), which I did not use to find these neurons.

The activations show that the three neurons do not all act the same way in absolute terms. L16 #180 is strongly negative (−1.8 for R0, −2.7 for R1). With a negative d·column, its write points toward the LaTeX regime on every prompt, so amplifying it pushes everything toward R1. L16 #3729 is positive and larger on R0 prompts (2.1 vs 1.3). Its contribution to the *difference* is pro-R1, but its absolute write points toward R0, so ×3 would push prompts toward R0. Ablating it is what removes a pro-R0 push. Before running, I'll check the sign of d·column for each neuron. If it confirms this reading, I'll revise the edit to: #180 ×3, #3621 ×3 if its write is pro-R1 in absolute terms, and #3729 ×0. Their activations average about 0 over answer tokens, so the edit should act mainly at the prompt, which is what I want.
